per_plume.source_hint: upper-level cloud filament / possible contrail over ocean west of central islands
evidence: Kilauea was erupting (Episode 54 of Halemaumau eruption began 10:30 HST Aug 25) while Mauna Loa was NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, so vog was possible in principle but must be downwind of the vents. [E1]

Plume centroid and wind-based upwind end (21.45N, -158.24W) are 382.9 km from Kilauea and 351.3 km from Mauna Loa to the NW, upwind of the Big Island under ENE flow (wind from 74 deg), inconsistent with vog trailing from either vent. [E5, E2]

Measured drift toward 64 deg at 40.8 km/h (fit R2 0.98) disagrees by ~180-190 deg with 10-m wind toward ~254 deg at centroid and ~245 deg at southern end (from 74 and 65 deg); disagreement well beyond 45 deg rules out low-level transport story and lowers confidence, favoring an upper-level cloud feature. [E4, E2, E7]
Inferred motion source end at 20.65N, -158.445W is 358.1 km from Kilauea and 323.8 km from Mauna Loa, providing no link to either vent. [E4]
No FIRMS fire clusters in box [-159,20,-157.5,21.8] around the plume on 2026-08-25; only Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal far away, arguing against wildfire smoke. [E6]

Mask is fully over ocean (land_frac 0.0, no islands swallowed) and is a thin 107-km, 1829 km2 filament described as translucent gray fainter than nearby white cumulus, morphology most consistent with thin high cloud/contrail rather than bright low cloud, vog, or smoke. [E3, E5]

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in July, while the summit region showed patterns of slight inflation. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 57 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the July reporting period, after 94 in June. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
